description: Automated bots scrape appointment systems in real time and capture slots en masse the moment they open, creating artificial scarcity. Reseller platforms openly advertise automated monitoring, instant alerts and auto-booking against VFS Global, TLScontact and BLS systems.
energy_note: Competing with software for a place in a queue.

description: TURSAB president Firuz Baglikaya said bots take the limited slots the moment the system opens, and appointments then sell for EUR 300-500, reaching EUR 1,000 in urgent cases. A visa services director told NTV some agents demand EUR 500-1,000, 'sometimes even as much as 3,000 euros'.
money_note: Black-market price for a free appointment.

description: VFS Regional Head for the UAE Monaz Billimoria said bots book slots the moment they are released, creating a 'false or forced limitation', with slots then sold outside at high prices when they are actually free on the VFS website.
energy_note: The provider confirms the market exists and cannot stop it.

aspect: The countermeasures, and their side effects
description: VFS deployed virtual keyboards, IP address restrictions, VPN blocking and a digital waiting room. VPN blocking is a particular problem for Iranians, who routinely need a VPN to reach blocked sites at all - the anti-bot measure locks out the legitimate user.
energy_note: Defended against, as a side effect of being Iranian.

description: Germany introduced a waiting-list system for short-stay Schengen applications on 18 March 2024, assigning appointments in the order applicants join, which the embassy says stops providers reserving slots in bulk.
energy_note: A fix that works, adopted by one country.

description: A viral protest movement over chronic appointment shortages, bot scalping, add-on fees, delayed passport returns and aggressive upselling of premium lounge services.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the official denial that helps nobody
description: Belgium's ambassador to Turkey said its system does not allow bots, urged applicants to use only VFS, and said unofficial agencies cannot get earlier access - 'This is wasted money.' Applicants who cannot find a slot are left choosing between an official channel with no availability and a broker officially described as a scam.
energy_note: Told the only route that works does not work.

aspect: The embassy sets the number, not the contractor
description: Embassies and consulates, not VFS, control how many appointments exist. The scarcity is a policy choice upstream of the company everyone blames.

There are no Schengen slots in Ankara for eleven weeks. A number circulating in a Telegram group offers an appointment in nine days for EUR 450, payable in advance to a Turkish account. Omid pays. The appointment is real. He never learns who the broker was or where the slot came from.
energy_note: Paying a stranger for something that is officially free.
